notes.aconitase_aco2_split_evidence: YALI1D11984g (YALI0D09361g, W29 XP_502616.2, UniProt Q6C9P6) is ACO1-type: PANTHER PTHR43160:SF3 aconitate hydratase, mitochondrial; 77.7 percent identity to S. cerevisiae Aco1p P19414 and 52.3 percent to Aco2p P39533. YALI1E17935g (YALI0E14949g, XP_503960.1, Q6C5V2) is ACO2-type: PANTHER PTHR43160:SF2 homocitrate dehydratase, mitochondrial; 70.3 percent identity to Aco2p and 54.9 percent to Aco1p (global alignment, BLOSUM62). S. cerevisiae Aco1p serves the citric acid cycle while Aco2p contributes only to lysine biosynthesis, and the Aco2 homologues of filamentous fungi were enzymatically inactive (Fazius 2012, PMID 23106124, abstract). Multicopy Y. lipolytica ACO1 shifts citric towards isocitric acid (Holz 2009, PMID 18850095, abstract; the locus is not named there). YALI1E17935g is therefore taken as homocitrate-specific or inactive, not as a citrate aconitase; it is not assigned to R24 (separate review). UniProt automatic names and GO terms call both proteins aconitate hydratase. Report reports/aconitase_aco2_split_20261029.
notes.aconitase_aco2_split_evidence_tier: homology (PANTHER subfamily, pairwise identity to the S. cerevisiae paralogs) plus S. cerevisiae and filamentous-fungal biochemistry; no Y. lipolytica enzymology, localisation or knockout for YALI1E17935g
